starting_points.name: Cargo binary package
starting_points.when: A new Rust service needs a new directory.
steps: Install the chosen Rust toolchain. Replace /path/to/workspace with the actual local source parent; choose the real package name.
Generate a binary package; use --lib only for a reusable library rather than an executable.
notes: A Cargo package is not a full framework application. Preserve generated defaults and add only selected dependencies.

starting_points.name: Cargo in an existing directory
starting_points.when: An existing source directory has no Cargo.toml and must become a package; choose this instead of cargo new.
steps: Inspect existing files and parent VCS before initialization; preserve existing code.

commands.purpose: Initialize a binary package in place.

notes: Use --lib for a library target. Do not run cargo init over an already initialized package.

follow_up_generators.name: SQLx migrations and checked-query metadata
follow_up_generators.when: Only when SQLx is selected and owns schema migrations; metadata applies when checked query macros are used.

commands.cwd: /path/to/workspace/project (DATABASE_URL targets a disposable database; migration SQL reviewed)
commands.purpose: Apply migrations to the disposable database.

commands.cwd: /path/to/workspace/project (checked query macros and matching disposable schema available)

notes: Install a selected sqlx-cli release compatible with the application and selected database/TLS features. Set DATABASE_URL through the environment or an untracked local file.
Preserve migrations and commit .sqlx metadata for offline builds. Run cargo sqlx prepare --check after changes; pass workspace/feature/target options matching the project.

preserve: Preserve Cargo.toml, generated source structure and Cargo.lock after dependency resolution for shipped applications. Record the chosen Rust toolchain and generator versions.

Retain the VCS ignore baseline when generated, including build-output exclusions, and add project-specific OS metadata/secret rules. Cargo VCS behavior depends on parent repository and configuration; inspect actual output.
Record and justify changes from the same-version generator baseline instead of recreating its files from memory.
Preserve SQLx migrations and offline query metadata when selected; keep database credentials out of version control.
verification: In the actual application, compare a fresh output from the recorded toolchain/options with the initial project and explain intentional differences.
After initial dependency resolution, run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test --locked and cargo build --locked from the package root; run the project-selected Clippy checks.
In a disposable copy, inspect git add --dry-run -A and confirm source/manifests/lockfile are included while target/, credentials and .DS_Store are excluded.
Cargo creates the package; Axum routing, Tokio runtime, configuration and shutdown remain explicit implementation. No full Axum application generator is asserted here.
For SQLx, test migrations in the disposable database and run cargo sqlx prepare --check with the same relevant features and targets.
integration_steps: After the selected Cargo baseline, add compatible Axum and Tokio dependencies; the documented examples are cargo add axum and cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread. Select required tower-http middleware explicitly.
Add SQLx with PostgreSQL, Tokio and the selected release's supported TLS configuration; install a compatible sqlx-cli release. Implement settings validation and a tracing subscriber.
Follow the selected SQLx migration instructions with DATABASE_URL pointing only to a disposable database. Write and review migration SQL before applying it; keep credentials outside tracked files.

For checked query macros, regenerate and commit .sqlx offline metadata after schema/query changes. Implement HTTP, real-database and cancellation tests, then run the profile verification checks with relevant features and targets.

Introduce Restate only after a separate restart/retry/idempotency proof. Pin the toolchain and release targets, preserve the application Cargo.lock after dependency resolution and qualify target/runtime/TLS dependencies. These application instructions were not executed.
